title: AERO9500 Final Report (Part 2) - Space Mission Design
overview: Design a simple space mission benefiting Australia and identify main elements of its space segment to demonstrate understanding of space segment systems (launch, orbits etc.) by developing a preliminary plan for a new mission using industry software and hand calculations.
deliverables: Technical report as single PDF containing mission design and all related work
Relevant screenshots embedded in report or appendix
All relevant STK or PIGI design files included in report/appendix

format.length: 20 pages max for core part (excluding title page, table of contents, references, etc.), concise
format.structure: Executive summary; Introduction - mission overview and rationale; Main body - all sections describing mission's space segment e.g. launch, orbit, ground stations, coverage, mission operation and end-of-life; Conclusion; Bibliography
format.other: Engineering report writing style: clear, effective, correct grammar/spelling. Figures and tables fully and correctly labelled with number, title and reference if necessary. All non-original text/diagrams/ideas cited and referenced, plagiarism-checked; Wikipedia not a proper source. Include software outputs.

requirements.text: Mission concept must benefit Australia in some way and be kept simple - examples: bushfire tracking and alert, weather satellite, internet/communication, earth observation for city planning/real estate.
State whether using one or multiple spacecraft and justify.
Define launch segment: where it will launch from and which launch vehicle.
Define orbit segment: type of orbit, its characteristics and orbital elements.
Determine if orbital maneuvers are required and detail them.
Define ground segment: which ground control facilities will be used and how often spacecraft can communicate with ground control / coverage analysis.
Define mission duration and plans for End-of-Life (EOL).

Use mission design software of choice to complete design (STK industry-standard, PIGI by Saber Astronautics - requires competition registration for license, or other like flightclub with prior approval) and supplement with hand calculations as needed.
